zh: 龜山島迷失於遠方雨霧
en: The rains of the northeast monsoon
Knocking against the stone terrace of the marine terrace
Rolling up scattered flecks of spray
Over the sea at Beiguan, mist and rain hang hazy
A few fishing boats rise and fall with wind and wave
Turtle Island lost in the distant rain and mist
The sea vast, the clouded sky boundless
Turtle Island, lost in fog
Faintly emerging from within the painting
A trace surfaces
A deja-vu kind of longing

zh: 隨半晦半明的月光起舞
en: Under the brush of Lan Yin-ding
Light and shadow flow and sway, mist and haze drift
Turtle Island, now visible, now hidden
Dancing with the moonlight, half dim, half bright

zh: 龜山島匍匐於墨綠海域
en: From the brush of Wang Pan-Youn
Dawn's red glow warms the edge of the sky
Turtle Island lies crouched upon the ink-green sea
Veiling loneliness and mystery

zh: 暮雲淡紫， 風平浪輕
遙對褚红岩石不著一語
暮靄雲天依然是飄渺雨霧
景色依稀， 思緖如縷
又豈是瞬間的潮起和潮落
en: From the brush of Chang Ping-tang
Evening clouds pale purple, wind calm, waves light
Turtle Island, still as a monk in meditation
Facing the rust-red rock from afar, saying not a word
The rhythm of the wind rises and falls on the sea's surface
The evening haze and clouded sky remain a faint, drifting mist of rain
Wherever the eye reaches
Scenery half-glimpsed, thoughts like fine threads
A life adrift and scattered
Like a solitary island upon the sea
At times jade mist and blue smoke curl about
After all
What is hidden has not disappeared
To be silent is not to have nothing to say
A lifetime's promise and regret
How could it be merely a moment's rise and fall of the tide
The glow of dusk vanishes without a trace?
And yet cannot be held back
Still is
Yesterday's dusk
Ripples fading into the distance
A vast, uncertain heart, blurred as mist and haze

points.zh: 龜山島，又稱龜山嶼，最早的名字叫煙斗嶼，頭城人常稱爲龜島或龜嶼。位於宜蘭蘭陽平原東面太平洋上，因外形似浮龜而得名。因蘭陽平原海岸線呈現弧形，龜山島樣貎會隨觀看地點而不同，有時可見整隻龜匍匐海面 (從頭城，北關一帶)，有時只見龜身，有時則呈三角形(從羅東，五結一帶)，因而出現「龜山轉頭」這樣出色的詞句。龜山島爲孤懸海外的火山島嶼，主要是由两座火山體組成龜頭和龜角，龜尾部位是一片細長的砂洲，隨潮水漲落，就像是烏龜擺尾。數萬年前曾經火山噴發，島上留有硫磺氣孔和溫泉。此外，距龜山島西南四公里，還有一個更小的「龜卵嶼」。龜山島以多變的容顏，始終守候着蘭陽平原，自古以來即與宜蘭人生息相關，是宜蘭人心靈生活的一部份，在沒有氣象預報之前，龜山島頂上是否聚集雲層，是宜蘭人判斷天氣的指针。透過攝影家的鏡頭，畫家的彩筆，設計家的巧思，文學家的描述，人們不斷發掘出龜山島豐㳍的生命力。龜山島不僅是宜蘭的自然地標，也代表了長久以來孕育而成的宜蘭意識。
points.en: Turtle Island, also called Guishan Islet, was originally named Pipe Islet; residents of Toucheng commonly call it Turtle Island or Turtle Islet. Located in the Pacific Ocean off the eastern side of the Lanyang Plain in Yilan, it takes its name from its resemblance to a floating turtle. Because the coastline of the Lanyang Plain curves, Turtle Island's apparent shape changes depending on the viewer's location — sometimes the whole turtle appears to lie flat on the water's surface (as seen from around Toucheng and Beiguan), sometimes only the turtle's body is visible, and sometimes it appears triangular (as seen from around Luodong and Wujie) — giving rise to the vivid phrase 'the turtle turns its head.' Turtle Island is a volcanic island isolated offshore, composed mainly of two volcanic bodies forming the turtle's head and horn, while the turtle's tail is a long, narrow sandbar that shifts with the tides, like a turtle swishing its tail. Tens of thousands of years ago the island experienced volcanic eruptions, and sulfur vents and hot springs remain on the island today. In addition, four kilometers southwest of Turtle Island lies an even smaller islet called 'Turtle Egg Islet.' With its ever-changing appearance, Turtle Island has always kept watch over the Lanyang Plain, and has been intertwined with the lives of the people of Yilan since ancient times, forming part of their spiritual life. Before weather forecasting existed, whether clouds gathered atop Turtle Island served as the compass by which the people of Yilan judged the weather. Through the lenses of photographers, the brushes of painters, the ingenuity of designers, and the writing of literary figures, people continue to uncover the rich vitality of Turtle Island. Turtle Island is not only a natural landmark of Yilan, but also represents the sense of Yilan identity that has been nurtured over a long span of time.

points.zh: 龜山島是台灣十大地景之一。爲了與聯合國教科文組織(UNESCO) 近年來力倡的地景保育理念接軌，台灣行政院林務局於2013年舉辦 「台灣十大地景」票選活動，由21萬民衆投票及學者專家評分，選出十大地景：1. 野柳，2. 玉山主峯，3. 日月潭，4. 金瓜石，5. 龜山島，6. 月世界泥岩惡地形，7. 雪山圈谷冰河遺迹，8. 清水斷崖，9. 苗栗三義火炎山自然保留區，10. 大霸尖山。
points.en: Turtle Island (Guishan Island) is one of Taiwan's Ten Great Landscapes. In order to align with UNESCO's recent advocacy of landscape conservation, Taiwan's Forestry Bureau (Executive Yuan) held a 'Taiwan's Ten Great Landscapes' vote in 2013; through the votes of 210,000 members of the public and the scoring of experts and scholars, the following ten landscapes were selected: 1. Yehliu, 2. Yushan Main Peak, 3. Sun Moon Lake, 4. Jinguashi, 5. Turtle Island, 6. Moon World Badlands (mudstone formations), 7. Xueshan Cirque Glacial Relics, 8. Qingshui Cliff, 9. Sanyi Huoyanshan Nature Reserve in Miaoli, 10. Da Ba Jian Mountain.

points.zh: 藍䕃鼎 (1903 -1979)，台灣知名水彩畫家，出生於宜蘭羅東。早年授教於日籍畫家石川欽一郎，他以水彩繪畫爲主要創作，以台灣本土的農村景色爲題材，一生堅持農村就是他的生命，始终走鄉村路綫。有「畫我故鄉的文化大使」的美譽，1971年，第一屆歐洲和第一屆美國藝術評論學會都選他爲「世界十大水彩畫家」之一。
points.en: Ran In-Ting (1903–1979), a renowned Taiwanese watercolor painter, was born in Luodong, Yilan. In his early years he studied under the Japanese painter Ishikawa Kin'ichirō. Working primarily in watercolor, he took the rural landscapes of his native Taiwan as his subject matter, insisting throughout his life that the countryside was his life's true calling, and he always kept to the path of rural themes. Known as the "cultural ambassador who paints my homeland," in 1971 he was selected by both the inaugural European and inaugural American art critics' associations as one of the "Ten Greatest Watercolor Painters in the World."

points.zh: 王攀元，國寳級畫家，1912生於江蘇，上海美術專科畢業，來台後任教於宜蘭羅東中學，與友人組成「蘭陽畫會」。蟄居蘭陽平原大半世紀，於2001年獲頒第五屆國家文藝奬，2013年獲第八屆噶瑪蘭獎。自幼失怙的王攀元，以繪畫映照一生的苦難，豪門遺孤的青春歲月，動盪流離的人生，都反映在其作品中，其創作即生命凝結的表現。在不同主題變奏裡，空，簡，淡，遠，始終是他低迴吟唱的主調，是欲語還留的獨白，是若隱若現的孤怨。具體又抽象，單純又深遠的畫面，縕藏着繁富的生命哲思。因其特有的超然畫風，而有「畫布上的詩人」之稱。
points.en: Wang Pan-yuan, a national treasure-class painter, was born in 1912 in Jiangsu, graduated from the Shanghai Academy of Fine Arts, and after coming to Taiwan taught at Luodong High School in Yilan, where he and friends formed the 'Lanyang Painting Society.' He lived in seclusion on the Lanyang Plain for most of a century, and in 2001 received the 5th National Award for Arts, and in 2013 the 8th Kavalan Award. Orphaned young, Wang Pan-yuan used painting to reflect a lifetime of hardship; the youth of an orphan from a once-great family, and a life of turmoil and displacement, are both reflected in his work — his creations are, in effect, the crystallization of his life. Across variations on different themes, emptiness, simplicity, plainness, and distance remain the recurring undertone he lingers over — a soliloquy half-spoken and half-withheld, a solitary resentment now visible, now hidden. His pictures, both concrete and abstract, both simple and profound, contain within them a rich philosophy of life. Because of his distinctively transcendent style, he has been called "the poet of the canvas."

points.zh: 張炳堂 (1928--2012) 台南人，14歲以一幅「大成坊」入選第7屆「台陽展」，躍居台灣最年輕的畫家。其後授教於郭柏川，並與廖繼春和顏水龍亦師亦友。個性耿介，堅持本土文化風格，終其一生居住台南，也許是南台灣的艷陽天氣使然，晚年在畫布上，以濃烈的原色，迸發來自陽光，土地的原生力量，以簡練的線條與快速的筆觸，一層又一層，揮灑出赤嵌樓，孔廟，運河，安平港等鄉土古典之美。是「向太陽借光，造心中之境，還鄉土之情。」如今，艶麗的廟宇紅牆和鮮黄湛藍的琉璃瓦，已經成爲張炳堂的標記。因其大紅，鮮綠，深藍的强烈色調畫風，而被稱為台灣野獸派的健將，但細觀其筆觸感動，又不失表現主義的豪放洒脱。
points.en: Chang Ping-tang (1928–2012), a native of Tainan, was selected for the 7th Taiyang Exhibition at age 14 with his work 'Dacheng Gate,' becoming Taiwan's youngest painter at the time. He later studied under Guo Bochuan and was both mentor-student and friend with Liao Chi-chun and Yen Shui-long. Of an upright and unyielding character, he insisted on a native local cultural style and lived his whole life in Tainan. Perhaps because of southern Taiwan's blazing sunny weather, in his later years he used intense primary colors on canvas, bursting forth with the elemental power of sunlight and land, using concise lines and swift brushstrokes to paint, layer upon layer, the classical local beauty of Chihkan Tower, the Confucius Temple, the canal, and Anping Harbor. It could be said he "borrowed light from the sun to build the landscape of his heart, and returned the affection owed to his native land." Today, the brilliant red walls of temples and the vivid yellow and blue glazed tiles have become Chang's signature. Because of his bold red, vivid green, and deep blue color schemes, he has been called a leading figure of Taiwanese Fauvism, but a close look at the emotion in his brushwork also reveals the bold, unrestrained spirit of Expressionism.
